speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to begin our assessment, have you experienced any severe headache, double vision, or difficulty speaking alongside your dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis (or potentially Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo given the brief 3-minute duration).

Please tell me: Did your dizziness change with specific head movements, or did it remain constant regardless of your position? Also, do you have any history of recent ear infections or head trauma?
